original.title: Matzo Ball Soup
original.description: A comforting Passover classic: light, fluffy matzo dumplings simmered in golden chicken soup with carrots and dill.
ingredients: 1/4 cup chicken broth or seltzer water
steps: Whisk the eggs, schmaltz or oil, and 1/4 cup broth or seltzer in a bowl.
Stir in the matzo meal, salt and pepper until just combined. Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes so the matzo meal can absorb the liquid.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
With wet hands, roll the mixture into 1-inch balls (they will double in size) and drop them into the boiling water.
Cover, reduce the heat to a steady simmer and cook for 30 to 35 minutes without lifting the lid, until the balls are fluffy and cooked through.
Meanwhile, simmer the chicken broth with the carrots, celery and onion for 20 minutes, until the vegetables are tender.
Add the shredded chicken, if using, and season the soup with salt and pepper.
Lift the matzo balls into the soup with a slotted spoon, sprinkle with dill and serve hot.

original.title: Charoset
original.description: A sweet apple, walnut and wine relish served at the Passover Seder to symbolize the mortar used by the Israelites in Egypt.
ingredients: 3 crisp apples, peeled and finely chopped
1/3 cup sweet red wine or grape juice
steps: Toss the chopped apples with the lemon juice in a bowl so they don't brown.
Add the walnuts, wine or grape juice, honey and cinnamon and stir well.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour so the flavors blend.
Stir again before serving with matzo.

original.title: Braised Beef Brisket
original.description: Tender, slow-braised brisket with onions and a tangy-sweet sauce — the centerpiece of many Passover and Hanukkah dinners.
ingredients: 1 cup dry red wine or more broth
steps: Preheat the oven to 325°F (165°C). Season the brisket all over with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven or roasting pan over medium-high heat and brown the brisket well on both sides, about 5 minutes per side. Remove to a plate.
Add the onions to the pan and cook for 10 minutes, stirring, until soft and golden. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute more.
Stir in the broth, wine, tomatoes, brown sugar, vinegar and bay leaves, scraping up the browned bits.
Return the brisket fat side up, spoon onions and sauce over it and tuck the carrots around it.
Cover tightly and braise in the oven for 3 to 3 1/2 hours, until fork-tender.
Let the brisket rest for 15 minutes, then slice thinly across the grain.
Skim the fat from the sauce and serve it spooned over the sliced meat. Brisket is even better made a day ahead and reheated in its sauce.

original.title: Potato Kugel
original.description: A golden, crisp-edged baked potato pudding, perfect for Passover and Shabbat dinners.
ingredients: 1/3 cup matzo meal or potato starch
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Pour 2 tbsp of the oil into a 9x13-inch baking dish and heat it in the oven.
Grate the potatoes and onion on the coarse side of a box grater or in a food processor.
Squeeze the grated potato and onion in a clean towel to remove as much liquid as possible.
Mix the potatoes and onion with the eggs, remaining oil, matzo meal, salt and pepper.
Carefully spread the mixture into the hot dish — it should sizzle.
Bake for 55 to 60 minutes, until deep golden and crisp on top.
Cut into squares and serve warm.

original.title: Flourless Chocolate Cake
original.description: A rich, fudgy chocolate cake made without flour — naturally gluten-free and kosher for Passover.
ingredients: Powdered sugar or berries, for serving
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Grease an 8-inch round cake pan and line the bottom with parchment paper.
Melt the chocolate and butter together in a bowl over simmering water or in the microwave in short bursts, stirring until smooth.
Whisk in the sugar and salt, then the eggs one at a time.
Sift in the cocoa powder, add the vanilla and whisk until just combined.
Pour into the pan and bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until the top has a thin crust and a toothpick comes out with moist crumbs.
Cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a plate.
Dust with powdered sugar and serve with berries or whipped cream.

original.title: Crispy Potato Latkes
original.description: Golden, lacy potato pancakes fried in oil for Hanukkah, served with applesauce and sour cream.
ingredients: 1/4 cup all-purpose flour or matzo meal
Applesauce and sour cream, for serving
steps: Grate the potatoes and onion using the coarse side of a box grater.
Wrap the mixture in a clean kitchen towel and squeeze out as much liquid as you can.
Mix the potatoes and onion with the eggs, flour, salt and pepper in a large bowl.
Heat about 1/4 inch of oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Drop heaping tablespoons of the mixture into the oil and flatten them slightly.
Fry for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until deep golden brown and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and sprinkle with a little more salt. Add more oil to the pan between batches as needed.
Serve hot with applesauce and sour cream.

original.title: Sufganiyot (Jelly Doughnuts)
original.description: Pillowy fried doughnuts filled with jam and dusted with sugar — a favorite Hanukkah treat.
steps: Stir the yeast and 1 tsp of the sugar into the warm milk and let stand 5 minutes until foamy.
Combine the flour, remaining sugar and salt in a bowl. Add the yeast mixture, eggs and butter and knead for 8 to 10 minutes into a soft, smooth dough.
Cover and let rise in a warm place for about 1 hour, until doubled.
Roll the dough 1/2 inch thick and cut 2 1/2-inch rounds. Place on a floured tray, cover and let rise 30 minutes.
Heat 2 inches of oil in a heavy pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the doughnuts a few at a time for 1 1/2 to 2 minutes per side, until deep golden. Drain on paper towels.
When cool enough to handle, poke a hole in the side of each doughnut and pipe in about 2 tsp of jam.
Dust generously with powdered sugar and serve the same day.

original.title: Chocolate Lava Cakes
original.description: Individual chocolate cakes with a warm, molten center — an easy, impressive Valentine's Day dessert for two or four.
ingredients: Butter and cocoa powder, for the ramekins
steps: Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Butter four 6-oz ramekins and dust them with cocoa powder.
Melt the chocolate and butter together and stir until smooth.
Whisk in the powdered sugar, then the eggs, yolks and vanilla.
Fold in the flour and salt until just combined.
Divide the batter among the ramekins and set them on a baking sheet.
Bake for 12 to 14 minutes, until the sides are firm but the centers still jiggle.
Let stand 1 minute, run a knife around the edges and invert onto plates.
Serve right away with ice cream or berries.

original.title: Chocolate-Dipped Strawberries
original.description: Fresh strawberries dipped in silky melted chocolate — a simple, elegant treat for Valentine's Day.
ingredients: 6 oz semisweet or dark chocolate, chopped
1 tsp coconut oil or vegetable shortening
steps: Rinse the strawberries and dry them completely — any water will make the chocolate seize.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Melt the chocolate with the coconut oil in a bowl over simmering water or in the microwave in 20-second bursts, stirring until smooth.
Holding each strawberry by the stem, dip it in the chocolate, let the excess drip off and place it on the parchment.
Melt the white chocolate, if using, and drizzle it over the berries with a fork.
Refrigerate for 20 to 30 minutes until set. Serve the same day.

original.title: Red Velvet Cupcakes
original.description: Soft, tender cocoa-kissed cupcakes with a rosy red crumb and tangy cream cheese frosting.
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk the flour, sugar, cocoa, baking soda and salt in a bowl.
In another bowl, whisk the oil, buttermilk, egg, food coloring, vanilla and vinegar.
Stir the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients until smooth.
Fill the liners two-thirds full and bake for 18 to 20 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool completely.
Beat the cream cheese and butter until smooth, then beat in the powdered sugar and vanilla until fluffy.
Pipe or spread the frosting on the cooled cupcakes.
